vram_estimate.reason: Ref2VA holds every reference's encoding resident beside the video latents, so the ceiling is a fixed base, a per-voxel term for the VAE decode's conv3d activation (width * height * num_frames), and a per-reference term. Classified against the 24 GB entry from the #479 field report (lem, RTX 3090 24 GB, int4 + 768p turbo LoRA, 9 steps, 2026-09-25/26) at 1344x768: 175 frames x 2 refs, 209 x 2 and 175 x 3 ran (projected 22.83, 23.77 and 23.83 GB); 209 x 3 OOM'd in reference encode needing a further 5.1 GB and 260 x 1 OOM'd at denoise step 1 needing a further 4.8 GB (projected 24.77 and 24.18 GB). The refused allocations are lower bounds, not peaks, so this is a classification with about 0.2 GB of margin either side, not a fitted curve. bytes_per_voxel is unchanged from #324's calibration (job 282172105da1); base_gb drops 0.3 GB now the references are counted separately. The cost entry's 42 min was that field run at 1344x768; re-priced to these 960x544 defaults it is 42 x 960*544 / (1344*768) = 21.2 (#866)
